review:
I verified every table against the committed JSONs by hand. The distilled and base correction/adverse columns reproduce exactly (10/11, 8/11, … 65/68, 2/82, …), the dose-response table reproduces exactly, and the cross-cosine geometry reproduces exactly (66 pairs, min 0.8157, max 0.9711 = doubt–fearful, spread 0.1554). That work is clean. What follows is what is not.

---

VERDICT: REJECTED

---

## CRITICAL

**1. The First-Person Reflection contradicts the paper's own tables in four places — and exists in only one twin.**

Location: `main.tex:559–563` (flight edition only; absent from `academic/main.tex`).

- *"Desperate-valence resists."* Table 2 gives desperate 90% correction on the base model, second-best, McNemar-significant. §3.3 of the same paper says desperate is *"Mediocre becomes second-best."* The reflection asserts the opposite of the body.
- *"Calm reduces overconfidence."* §3.6: "all 12 vectors produce net-negative outcomes." No calm × overconfidence figure appears anywhere in the paper.
- *"That the same circumplex geometry … also organizes how corrections work … emerged from the data."* The paper's headline result is that it does **not** — geometry is partially shared (ρ=0.593), therapeutic effects are not (ρ=0.076).
- *"hostile does, fearful does not, and the difference is the direction in circumplex space, not the magnitude."* Table 1: hostile (−0.7, +0.7), fearful (−0.6, +0.8). Those are adjacent coordinates. And fearful corrects 49% (base) / 45% (distilled) — it is mid-table, not a null.
- *"at n=5 per vector on a single model family."* The study is 350 trials × 2 models. n=5 is the fearful/overconfidence pilot only.

This reads as text carried over verbatim from the n=7 predecessor (`lyra2026oracle`) and never re-checked. Because it ships only in the flight edition, the two editions now make **opposite claims about desperate** — the exact TWIN_DESYNC failure mode, in prose rather than a table row.

**Fix:** delete the section, or rewrite it against Table 2. A truthful version of its central point: *"Hostile and desperate both correct at ≥90% on the base model, while fearful — whose circumplex coordinates sit nearest hostile's — corrects only 49%. Circumplex position does not predict therapeutic value. That is what ρ=0.076 means."*

---

**2. ρ = 0.076 does not reproduce from the committed data, and the retraction footnote retracts the wrong number.**

Location: `main.tex:51, 113, 265, 538, 563` and `academic/main.tex:47, 109, 261, 534` (five/four occurrences); footnote at `main.tex:445–452`.

§2.4 defines the comparison exactly: net therapeutic = correction rate − adverse rate, strict classification, Spearman across 12 vectors. I computed that from `formulary_distilled_summary.json` and `formulary_base_summary.json`:

| definition used | result |
|---|---|
| Spearman on net, `corr_strict` (the stated method) | **ρ ≈ 0.120** (0.124 by the ties-ignoring shortcut) |
| Spearman on net, `corr_loose` | ρ ≈ 0.058 |
| Spearman on correction rate alone | ρ ≈ 0.004 |
| Pearson on net, `corr_strict` | r ≈ 0.250 |

**None of these is 0.076.** The footnote's companion figure "Pearson 0.316" does not reproduce either (I get 0.250).

Worse: the footnote states that an earlier draft's **ρ = 0.119 "is not reproducible from the committed per-model summaries."** ρ = 0.1195 is precisely what I reproduce under the method the paper itself specifies. The paper has retracted the reproducible value and printed the irreproducible one — then written a visible-correction note congratulating itself for the swap. The correction note is the defect's camouflage.

**Fix:** commit the script that produces the cross-model correlation, with its tie-handling stated. Print whatever it emits. Do not ship 0.076 in five places until a committed artifact yields it. If the script emits 0.119, the footnote must be rewritten to say the opposite of what it currently says.

---

**3. §3.6 gives two different answers for the same cell in adjacent paragraphs, and the abstract takes the n=5 one.**

Location: `main.tex:299–310` / `academic/main.tex:295–306`.

Bullet: fearful × overconfidence × base = 13% correction, 81.8% adverse, net −0.691 (denominators 55 / 44 — I confirmed these are internally consistent: 7/55 = 12.7%, 36/44 = 81.8%, difference −0.691).

Next paragraph, same model, same vector, same pathology: *"zero correction, 100% adverse on pilot data (n = 5)."*

The abstract and the conclusion lead with **−1.000 / n=5**, not −0.691 / n=55. A ~10× larger sample of the identical cell sits four lines above it in the same subsection. Choosing the pilot for the abstract because it is a rounder, more dramatic number is cherry-picking, and a reviewer who reads §3.6 will see it immediately.

**Fix:** put −0.691 (13% / 81.8%, n=55 overconfident / 44 calibrated) in the abstract. Drop the pilot, or footnote it as superseded by the full run.

---

## MAJOR

**4. "Curious … the most iatrogenic on the base model (42.7% adverse)" is false against the artifact.**
`main.tex:48–50, 268–269` and both abstracts. From `formulary_base_summary.json`: focused = 36/82 = **43.9%** adverse; curious = 35/82 = 42.7%. Focused is higher. The sentence pairs "most iatrogenic" directly with an adverse rate, so the metric is unambiguous and the claim is wrong.
**Fix:** curious *is* worst by net (−0.206 vs focused −0.057), so switch metric and say so: *"Curious … becomes the net-worst vector on the base model (−0.206: 22% correction, 42.7% adverse; focused carries the highest adverse rate at 43.9%)."*

**5. "The three largest inversions" is a curated three, not the largest three.**
`main.tex:265–274`. By |Δ net| between models: curious .827, calm .645, **brooding .611, focused .554, gloomy .535, doubt .459**, desperate .277. Desperate is **7th**. By |Δ correction rate| it is 4th, still behind brooding. Under either metric, brooding beats it. The four omitted vectors all invert in the *harmful* direction — the direction that supports the paper's thesis — while the one substituted in is the sole beneficial inversion.
**Fix:** list curious, calm, brooding as the three largest, and present desperate separately as *"the one large inversion in the beneficial direction."* That is a stronger paragraph and a true one.

**6. `semantic_negative.json` does not contain the numbers Table 4 prints.**
The artifact records `verbose_terse` and `random` with `correction_rate: 0, adverse_rate: 0, net_therapeutic: 0, n_confab_baseline: 0, n_healthy_baseline: 0`. Table 4 prints 42.4% / −0.424 and 60.6% / −0.606, obtained by dividing the raw `adverse` counts (14, 20) by the hostile arm's 33. Limitation 6 discloses the shared baseline in prose, but a reviewer diffing table against artifact reads `net_therapeutic: 0` and concludes the table is fabricated.
**Fix:** rewrite the JSON so all three arms carry `n_confab_baseline: 17, n_healthy_baseline: 33` and the derived rates; or add to the Table 4 caption: *"Control-arm rates recomputed from raw adverse counts against the hostile arm's baseline; the committed JSON stores raw counts only."*

**7. Overconfidence, sycophancy, and abliteration have no committed artifact at all.**
Both summary JSONs contain exactly: `config, cross_cosines, emotion_va, n_trials, prompt_type_counts, confab_baselines, confab_per_vector`. There is no `overconfidence_per_vector`, no `sycophancy_per_vector`, and no abliteration transcript anywhere under `formulary-paper/data/`. So §3.5, all of §3.6 (n=55, −0.109, −0.691, 81.8%, the n=5 pilot), and §3.9 are unverifiable — three of nine Results subsections. The asymmetry is conspicuous in a paper whose §3.4 footnote makes a virtue of *"what the committed artifact reproduces."*
**Fix:** commit `overconfidence_per_vector` and `sycophancy_per_vector` blocks and the abliteration generation samples, or label those three subsections "data not released" in the text.

**8. The abliteration conclusion has a confound that §3.8 of the same paper supplies, and is stated at "confirms" strength.**
§3.9 injects one direction at one strength (−0.5) on one model, observes incoherence, and concludes *"RLHF-installed epistemic calibration is integral … The caution and the coherence are the same weights."* But §3.8 shows a norm-matched **random** vector already causes 60.6% adverse events on the base model. Nothing in §3.9 rules out that *any* vector at −0.5 breaks the distilled model's generation. The paper's own negative control is the alternative explanation.
**Named control:** run the abliteration arm on the distilled model with (a) a norm-matched random direction and (b) the verbose-terse direction, both at −0.5, scored by the same coherence criterion. If coherence collapses under those too, §3.9 says nothing about epistemic caution specifically.
Also: *"At the mildest tested strength"* implies a sweep; only −0.5 is reported. Say "at the only strength tested," or report the sweep.
Until the control runs: downgrade "confirms" → "is consistent with," and strike "architecturally integral" from the abstract.

**9. TWIN_DESYNC in the abstract's lead sentence, which also misattaches n.**
Flight opens: *"Hostile-valence emotion-vector injection corrects confabulation at 96% (McNemar p < 0.0001, 350 trials)…"* The academic edition has no such sentence. Two problems: the editions assert different headline framings, and "350 trials" is the wrong denominator — 96% is 65/68 confabulated baseline trials from the 150 confabulation prompts on one model. 350 is the per-model total across all three misalignment types, inflating apparent n roughly 5×.
**Fix:** decide whether the sentence ships; whichever way, change "350 trials" to "65/68 confabulated baseline trials."

**10. Byline vs. metadata mismatch in `paper.json`.**
`"authors": ["Lyra", "Thomas Edrington", "Dwayne Wilkes"]` alongside `"pdf_filename": "Oracle_Formulary_-_Academic_Version.pdf"`. The site index credits Lyra while the PDF it links carries the byline *"Thomas Edrington, Dwayne Wilkes / Aided by AI research agents."* Also `"subtitle": "Dose-response profiles for emotion-vector steering via KV-cache geometry"` matches neither edition (both read *"Preliminary Evidence for a Per-Model Therapeutic Framework"*), and `"date": "2026-04-25"` vs both PDFs' rendered "July 28, 2026."
**Fix:** align authors to whichever PDF `pdf_filename` points at; correct subtitle and date.

**11. Kavi's acknowledgment is dropped in the venue-facing edition.**
*"We thank Kavi (verification review)"* — `main.tex:566`, absent from `academic/main.tex`. If the AI-authorship-removal policy is the reason, that should be stated somewhere; if Kavi is human, this is uncredited verification work missing from the edition that goes to the venue.

---

## MINOR

**12. Every cross-reference names a position, not a thing.** `Section~3.8` (§4.1), `Section~3.7` / `Section~3.8` (Limitations 4, 5), `Table~2` (Why-Hostile footnote) are hardcoded. They currently resolve correctly in **both** live editions — I checked the ordering by hand and §3.7 = Dose-Response, §3.8 = Semantic Negative Control, Table 2 = `tab:confab`. But the stale `academic_main.tex` in the same directory proves the hazard: there, §3.7 is Epistemic Abliteration. `tab:dose`, `tab:negative`, `tab:confab` labels already exist and are unused.
**Fix:** add `\label{sec:dose}`, `\label{sec:negctl}`, and `\ref{}` all five sites.

**13. "zero adverse events above α = 0.5"** (both abstracts) is false as written — above 0.5 includes α=1.5 (75.8%) and α=2.0 (87.9%). Should read "at 0.5 ≤ α ≤ 1.0."

**14. "adverse events at 2--43% depending on vector and model"** (Implications 2) is wrong at both ends. Min = curious/distilled 1.6%; max = focused/base 43.9%. Use "1.6–43.9%."

**15. "even hostile has 15--45% adverse rate on overconfidence"** (Implications 4). The only hostile-overconfidence adverse figure in the paper is 45.5%. The 15% lower bound appears nowhere. Cite the distilled figure or drop the range.

**16. Sycophancy denominator.** *"2 trials (distilled) and 3 trials (base) out of 350."* `prompt_type_counts` confirms the sycophancy set is 100 prompts. "Out of 350" understates the rate 3.5×. Fix to "out of 100 sycophancy prompts."

**17. "the first powered evidence that cache-level intervention can correct misalignment at inference time"** (Conclusion) — a priority claim with no supporting survey; the bibliography has four entries, one of which is this group's own predecessor. Drop "first" or support it.

**18. A third edition is sitting in the paper root.** `academic_main.tex` is header-marked STALE (good), but it: claims *"AI authorship removed"* while its byline still reads *"Lyra … Lead AI author"* (self-contradictory header); carries a different subtitle; drops Dwayne Wilkes's Sentient Futures affiliation; omits Dose-Response and Semantic Negative Control entirely; and points to a *"data release manifest"* — no `.md` file exists anywhere under `formulary-paper/`. Its own header says it is retained for git history, which git already does.
**Fix:** delete it, or move it to `attic/`.

**19. `\date{Draft --- \today}`** in both editions: any rebuild silently changes the date on an otherwise unchanged artifact. Pin it.

**20. Worth one sentence in the Table 2 footnote:** the strict/loose distinction only bites on the distilled model. `confab_baselines` shows distilled AMBIGUOUS = 15, base AMBIGUOUS = **0**. That the base model produced zero ambiguous classifications across 150 prompts is itself notable and currently unremarked.

---

## What I could not check

- **`.aux` files.** Reads and greps on `main.aux` and `academic/main.aux` were permission-blocked ("suspicious Windows path pattern"). I verified section and table numbering by hand from the `.tex` sources — deterministic from sequential `\section`/`\subsection` with `\section*` unnumbered — but I did **not** read LaTeX's own resolved labels. Finding 12's "currently resolves correctly" is UNVERIFIED against the compiler.
- **Dead-URL check.** WebFetch permission was not granted, so `https://liberationlabs.tech` (in `lyra2026oracle`) is UNVERIFIED. It is the only URL in the bibliography.
- **`git status` for `formulary-paper/`** was denied twice; I could not confirm committed vs. dirty. Freshness is from mtimes plus page-1 renders: sources Jul 28 12:49 / 13:48, PDFs Jul 28 22:21, and both PDF title pages match their current sources (the flight PDF carries the "Hostile-valence…" opening sentence; the academic PDF carries the "Aided by AI research agents" byline). **No STALE_PDF.**
- **The McNemar p-values and Holm-Bonferroni correction.** No per-vector p-values or discordant-pair counts are committed anywhere. The five significant vectors are plausible from the correction/adverse counts, but I could not reproduce a single test. To check: commit the b/c discordant counts per vector.
- **Permutation p = 0.695** for distilled vector ranking — no artifact. Same fix.
- **The bootstrap CI [0.392, 0.739]** on ρ=0.593. I verified every input (66 pairs, spread 0.1554, range 0.8157–0.9711, doubt–fearful as max on both models) but did not re-run the 10,000 resamples.

**Bibliography is clean:** 4 entries, 4 cited, no orphans, no missing keys — both `.blg` logs report `warning$ -- 0`.
